Order 
This is first application under Section 482 of Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita has been filed on behalf of the applicant for grant of anticipatory bail.

2. Applicant is apprehending her arrest in connection with RCT No.1239/2024 of Police Station,
Saman, District-Rewa for commission of the offences punishable 419, 420, 467, 471 and 120-B read with section 34 of IPC.
3.
Prosecution story in brief is that applicant in collusion with other co-accused persons got fraudulently sale-deed registered with respect to complainant's property by impersonating complainant.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is a bona fide purchaser.
It is urged that after purchasing property, applicant filed an application for mutation and notice was issued thereon.

After receipt of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:63249 2 MCRC-47503-2025 notice,
complainant appeared and informed that she did not sale any property.
Thereafter, complainant filed an application before the SHO, PS Mangawan, Distt. Rewa (Anexure A/2).
It is urged that when complainant took objection at the time of mutation proceedings, then, applicant came to know that he has been defrauded.
Applicant made a complaint before police station but no FIR has been registered.
Similarly, complainant also made a complaint before the PS but no FIR has been registered.
Then, complainant filed the present complainant case.

It is also urged that in the instant Deepika Tiwari vs Pushpa Dwivedi on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28380338/
1 case, original documents have not been filed, still, cognizance has been taken in the instant case for the offence under Sections 467, 468 and 471 etc.

sentences.text: Trial Court was required to issue at the first instance summons, then, bailable warrant and thereafter, arrest warrant could have been issued.
On above grounds, it is urged that applicant be granted the benefit of anticipatory bail.
5. Heard.
Perused the record of the case.

6. Perusal of record of the case reveals that trial Court has taken cognizance against applicant as well as other persons vide order dated 15.7.2024 for offence under sections 419, 420, 467, 468 and 120-B of IPC.

It is also evident from order sheet dated 15.7.2024 that applicant has not been given any notice and they have not been heard prior to taking of cognizance whereas as per proviso 1 to section 223 of BNSS, trial Court was mandatorily required to give an opportunity of hearing to applicants before NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:63249 3 MCRC-47503-2025 taking of cognizance but aforesaid provisions have not been followed by the trial court.
7.

In view of aforesaid and overall facts and circumstances of the case but without expressing any opinion on the merit of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which applicant may be released on bail.
Consequently, anticipatory bail application filed on behalf of applicant stands allowed.

8. It is directed that in the event of her arrest, applicant be released on bail on her furnishing a personal bond of Rs.15,000/- (Rupees Fifteen Thousand Only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer.

9. It is also directed that applicant shall abide by the conditions as enumerated under Section 482(2)
of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.

It is made clear that applicant shall appear before the Investigating Officer as & when she is so directed and cooperate with the investigation and she shall also appear before the Trial Court failing which her bail shall automatically stand cancelled without further reference to the Court.
10. C.C. as per rules.

(ACHAL KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE vai Deepika Tiwari vs Pushpa Dwivedi on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28380338/
